transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-30
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Leila Mendez (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood CSM), Amir Banerjee (CTO, Ceres), Sofia Ruiz (Head of ML), Dylan Price (Infra), Hannah Lee (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy):
Ceres wants low-latency embed + chat across EU + NA, strict encryption controls, prefer customer-managed keys, want pilot on Dedicated with potential private deployment later. Next steps are security docs, runbook draft, sample prompts and perf tests.

00:00 Jordan: okay uh good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood inference, i'm the AE, with me is our se leila and priya from success. how's everyone doing?
00:08 Amir: hey hey doing good thanks, little delayed in seattle but all good.
:15 Sofia: hi team, excited to jump in — we had a few pre-quals in the notes but happy to go deeper.

01:02 Jordan: quick agenda — intro, where you are today, constraints, decide pilot scope, then action items. we want to make sure we cover security and the runtime options cause i know you have regs in eu.
01:18 Amir: yep, data residency is the big one. we can't have user pii leave EU zone. also need SAML sso and company-managed keys.
01:30 Leila: okay good — we definitely support SAML and KMS, we have patterns for VPC private deployments and also dedicated reserved pools. quick question: is the initial pilot internal only or external customer-facing?
01:45 Sofia: internal to start, for triage automation in our support flows, so lower qps but sub-200ms p50 latency target for short chats would be ideal.
02:05 Dylan: for infra, we're running on GCP europe-west1 and have VPC peering requests open. we'd prefer not to open public egress for the pilot, so private connectivity is preferred.

03:00 Leila: great — sounds like Dedicated in-region or Private VPC deployment. tradeoffs: hosted API is fastest on-boarding but then you'd need to accept cross-region handling, dedicated gives isolation + reserved throughput, private lets you keep control of network and KMS but is heavier ops.
03:22 Amir: leaning to dedicated but with customer-managed KMS; we need the keys in our HSM or cloud-kms. how's that typically handled?
03:36 Leila: we can integrate with your cloud KMS — store encryption keys customer-side, Redwood supports envelope encryption; we'll send integration notes. there are some network config steps for the key exchange.
03:50 Jordan: also can share our SOC2 and ISO docs — we'll drop those in the drive.

05:10 Priya: quick note on roles — i'll be your success lead for the pilot, leila will run the perf and infra checks, jordan will coordinate contracts/pricing.
05:24 Hannah: perfect. timeline question: what's a realistic ramp to pilot? two to three weeks?
05:36 Jordan: with docs in hand i'd say 2–4 weeks to pilot depending on networking approvals; the VPC peering often is the blocker.
05:48 Dylan: yep peering + firewall rules is our usual delay. we can prioritize the ticket.

07:00 Leila: let's talk metrics for success — Sofia? what are must-haves vs nice-to-haves?
07:12 Sofia: must-haves: p50 latency <250ms for 64-token responses, throughput to handle 50 concurrent internal sessions, 99.9% availability during business hours. nice-to-have: prefix caching to lower cost on repeated queries and token-level cost breakdowns.
07:36 Leila: good — caching and batching configs can be part of Optimize recommendations. we'll propose batching window and KV cache settings after we see the sample prompts.

09:10 Jordan: any legal/compliance needs — Amir?
09:16 Amir: yep we have an internal data-handling policy and external auditor. need audit logs, retention controls, SSO with SCIM, and encryption at rest (customer-managed keys). also need to review subprocessors.
09:35 Jordan: understood — we'll include audit-log retention options and subprocessors list.

11:00 Leila: technical deep-dive needed later on: model choices and quantization. Sofia mentioned cost-sensitivity?
11:12 Sofia: yes, cost per 1k tokens matters — we'd rather tune quantization than move to smaller model that loses accuracy. we want to see lat/price tradeoffs.
11:28 Leila: we'll run a perf matrix with a few verified open models — include quantized variants and measure p50/p95 and token cost estimates.
11:40 Amir: can you run a baseline test from our region to estimate network overhead?
11:47 Leila: yes, we'll do a latency probe and synthetic token test — need an API endpoint that we supply for the smoke tests.

14:00 Jordan: inventory of deliverables — i'll send SOC2 and network diagram, leila sends perf template, you (sofia) send prompts. we'll set CR on the pilot size.
14:20 Dylan: quick ops question — what ports/protocols for the VPC peering? do you need NAT?
14:30 Leila: no NAT ideally; we'll provide minimal firewall rules, and a specific CIDR for peering. we'll share a runbook snippet with the required routes.

16:00 Sofia: also curious about model rollouts — can we do canary on model version and automatic fallbacks?
16:12 Leila: yes, Redwood supports rollout policies: canary, A/B, with auto-fallback to a cheaper variant if latency spikes. we'll demo the Console controls in the next session.
16:30 Amir: great, want to see the tracing and token-level cost breakdown before commit.

18:00 Jordan: pricing note — pilot pricing will be usage-based for hosted, but for Dedicated we can propose a small reserved pool for the pilot month to guarantee throughput. we'll send a short estimate table.
18:18 Amir: okay helpful. also curious if you support VPC cross-region fallbacks in case of capacity issues?
18:28 Leila: yes, policy-based routing can failover to a different region or model variant; we'll show that in the ops doc.

20:00 Jordan: any competitors in your evaluation?
20:06 Hannah: we're also evaluating Anthropic for safety features and Vertex AI for integration with our GCP infra, and a small proof-of-concept with OpenAI.
20:20 Jordan: fair. we'll focus on production economics and the SSO/KMS story as differentiators.

22:00 Priya: scheduling — proposing a Dedicated runtime walkthrough (60m) with infra team next tues or wed. does that work?
22:12 Dylan: wed works for me, tuesday is tight.
22:20 Leila: i'll send an invite for Wed 2025-04-09 10am CET unless anyone objects.

24:00 Sofia: one more: runbook expectations — we'd like a runbook skeleton including escalation paths, runbook owner, metrics dashboard links.
24:10 Priya: absolutely — we'll draft the runbook and share a workspace link, hope to have first draft in 5 business days.

26:00 Jordan: recap — action items: docs (SOC2, KMS, network), sample prompts, perf template, schedule deep-dive. everyone okay?
26:08 Amir: yes, sounds good.
26:15 Sofia: okay thanks all.

28:00 (cross talk)
28:15 Leila: small comment — for the KV cache we may recommend a 60s eviction for chat to help P50 without blowing cost.
28:28 Sofia: noted.

30:00 Jordan: last question — any contractual blockers we should know? procurement timeline?
30:10 Amir: procurement sits on a quarterly cycle, but for internal pilot procurement is light, we can do a memorandum of understanding. if pilot shows value we'll move to formal contract in Q2.
30:30 Jordan: perfect — that gives us runway.

32:00 Jordan: ok we'll wrap, thanks everyone. we'll send notes and the first set of docs by end of day monday.
32:12 Dylan: thanks, bye.
32:15 Hannah: bye all.

Transcription notes: occasional mis-attributed speaker lines, some timestamps approximate. Some technical terms may be slightly mangled (HSM/KMS spelled correctly mostly).

Attachments & links referenced: shared drive link (redwood/sales/ceres2025) — Jordan to populate; perf template (redwood/eng/perf/pilot-template.xlsx); runbook skeleton (redwood/templates/runbook.md).
